recipe: Thermal governor with a four-sample debounce for vLLM
note: Every entry is a transcription made by the studio. The basis field is the studio's original wording; read it with the label in the recipe: an entry without a published raw file is REPORTED, whatever its basis says.

receipts.claim: Software pacing lines of the engine scheduler
receipts.value: pause at 90 C, resume at 86 C, latch at 91 C or thermal margin 1 C or less; poll every 0.25 s; at most 120 s per pause episode
receipts.caveat: Operating guardrails chosen by the owner, not manufacturer limits. The card's own protections are untouched: 92 C maximum operating point, slowdown at margin -2 C, shutdown at margin -5 C.

receipts.value: a single sample (88 C, margin 1.0 C, out of line with its neighbours) latched the guard, killed the engine and dropped the in-flight requests
receipts.caveat: Temperature and margin are two separate NVML calls, so one glitchy pair can look like an emergency. One incident; no count of earlier false latches.

receipts.value: latch after 4 consecutive bad samples (about 1 s at the poll rate); immediate latch for thermal slowdown, margin -1 C or less, or 92 C and above; minimum hold of 2 s once paused; never resume above the resume line
receipts.caveat: Cost: a real 91 C condition needs about 0.75 to 1 s to latch.

receipts.claim: Staging in real vLLM 0.32.0 with injected samples
receipts.value: 7 of 7 injected cases behaved as designed: lone bad sample no latch; scattered bad no latch; three bad then good no latch; minimum hold measured 2.053 s; four in a row latched with HTTP 500 and failed health within 1 s; thermal slowdown latched at once and the engine exited within 1 s
receipts.caveat: Injected samples were synthetic; real card peak 83 C. Immediate latches at margin -1 and 92 C were covered by unit tests, not by the engine run. A 9B model at 8192 context, not the 262,144-token profile.

receipts.value: 37 pass at promotion; 43 pass after speculative-decoding support was added
receipts.caveat: CPU tests with a fake clock and sensor. They do not prove live recovery from every fault or an absolute temperature ceiling.

receipts.value: during a hold the scheduler zeroes the per-step token budget, so the base scheduler schedules nothing; no KV allocation, no preemption, pending draft tokens untouched
receipts.caveat: Read from the vLLM 0.32.0 scheduler, engine core and model runner code, plus the unit test; async scheduling and overlapping batches are refused because draft bookkeeping across steps was not inspected. The module is pinned to that exact vLLM version.

receipts.value: a latched fault raises inside the engine so health fails and the supervisor restarts it; there is no silent resume after a timeout
receipts.caveat: It cannot interrupt a kernel already on the GPU or a blocking NVML call; an external guard is still needed for tests.

receipts.claim: Harness mistake 1: stopping a run because the other card was hot
receipts.value: a staging run was cut at 85 s when the other card reached 90 C under a consumer's load; the harness treated it like its own stop line
receipts.caveat: Fixed so the other card stops a test at 91 C after 4 consecutive 1 Hz samples, or at once on margin 1 C or less, slowdown or 92 C.

receipts.claim: Harness mistake 2: a pause that did not pause
receipts.value: sending the stop signal to a process group missed the worker (it runs in its own session): 98.7% utilisation and 297 W during 77 "paused" samples
receipts.caveat: Fix: signal the whole process tree; verified live: utilisation 100% to 4%, power 300 W to 116 W, 88 C to 83 C within about four seconds of a stop.

receipts.claim: Harness mistake 3: a status check that matched the wrong text
receipts.value: the initial launch aborted after 2 s because "Not Active" contained the substring the check looked for

receipts.claim: Does the pause line work under load?
receipts.value: not observed on the 262,144-token profile: six minutes of 16-stream decode at the 300 W limit plateaued at 87 to 88 C (monitor peak 89 C) and never reached 90 C
receipts.caveat: So a real hold-and-resume with MTP drafts pending is unknown. An operator note (date not recorded) says the scheduler holds several times a day in normal serving: that is REPORTED, with no count behind it, and the Week 3 GPU 0 daily maxima of 80 to 82 C from 2026-11-08 sit under the 90 C pause line.

receipts.value: in-engine scheduler 90 C / 86 C; external test harness 88 C pause / 84 C resume; image pool 88 C / 84 C; own-work stop 91 C everywhere
receipts.caveat: Lines differ by layer on purpose: the external harness acts earlier so the in-engine pause is the backstop.

receipts.value: safe operation "at 90 C"; behaviour at other ambient temperatures; hold-and-resume under real load with drafts; a long-run count of pauses
receipts.caveat: The lines are guardrails the owner chose; this recipe does not claim they are safe limits.
